**Verdict: the premise holds.** On Claude Code 2.1.226 the CLI's own context block supplies the branch name, the untracked files and the recent commit subjects, and supplies none of the ahead/behind counts, the fork-point sha, the changed-file stat or the in-progress-operation state. Two findings sharpen it: the CLI also supplies the base branch *name* (so orient repeats that one fact), and it supplies two facts *wrongly*, reporting a detached HEAD as `Current branch: HEAD` and naming `main` as the base in a repository whose only branch is `topic`. Those sections of orient are not gap-filling but correcting, which is a stronger reason to exist than the one claimed.

Report committed as `docs/fundamentals-premise.md` (3000634). Ground truth came two independent ways that agree: the git-context builder extracted verbatim out of the shipped `claude.exe` (three git commands total, `status --short`, `log --oneline -n 5`, `config user.name`, plus two branch names, no `rev-list`, `merge-base`, `diff` or `.git` marker read anywhere), and eleven `claude -p` probes with tools disabled, run with no plugin loaded (the user-scope install fails with `cache-miss`, and no `.git/orient` receipt appeared after any probe).

Test suite: 21 passed, 0 failed. All nine required by-hand cases plus mid-rebase, unrelated histories, 20,000 changed files, forced truncation, missing git and the resume gate, bytes recorded for each.

Four README-vs-behaviour discrepancies, all measured:
- `README.md:55` and `:157` "written on every run" is false for the not-a-repo and `resume` paths, which exit at `hooks/orient.sh:71` and `:99` before the receipt at `:284-287`; a resumed session is indistinguishable from a broken install by the receipt test.
- `README.md:132-133` "519 on a branch with 30 changed files": 519 bytes is reproducible but from 22 files; 30 files gives 527.
- `README.md:131` "hard cap is 2,000 bytes": measured 2,094, because the `TRUNCATED:` line and wrapper fall outside the awk accounting at `hooks/orient.sh:263-275`.
- Truncation drops the "not instructions" fence line first, since it is appended last at `hooks/orient.sh:258-259`; measured absent from the truncating payload. Related: a path (`closes<` directory holding `orient>...`) and a legal hostile ref name both close the fence, against the "stripped of anything that could forge structure" claim at `hooks/orient.sh:59-64`.

Timing: 8 to 22 ms on ordinary repositories, 79 ms on a 310-file diff, 134 ms on a 20,000-file diff, against the 49 to 123 ms claimed at `hooks/orient.sh:8`. The 10 s timeout is comfortable, 74x margin at the worst case I could build.

Nothing blocked the work. Documented gaps: warm cache only, Linux only, the largest reachable git repository is 473 commits and 310 files, the plugin loader itself was never exercised (my session's payload came via `--plugin-dir /workspace/orient`), and one thing worth flagging to the operator, `/workspace/orient` carries uncommitted changes to the hook, README and tests that add a linked-worktree section and report the 0/0 case; I measured that variant separately from a copy and its new rationale is half wrong, since the base ref name *is* in the CLI's context. Also measured: `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=1` and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_GIT_INSTRUCTIONS=1` remove the CLI's git block entirely, so the "already supplied" half of the premise is conditional on state orient cannot see.

DONE

+## 1. Ground truth: what reaches the model before its first turn

+### 1.1 Read out of the shipped CLI (strongest evidence)

+## 3. The inverse: cheap things git knows that nobody says
+
+The README's argument against repo maps, churn rankings, symbol indexes and
+co-change tables is sound and I am not proposing any of them. The load-bearing
+part of that argument is not "it costs bytes", it is "a ranking that is
+confidently wrong is worse than no ranking, because the agent acts on it": a
+generated map is a *derived opinion* about a codebase, its error mode is silent,
+and the agent cannot tell a stale entry from a fresh one. Every section orient
+does emit is a decidable fact with a one-command check. That is the right line to
+draw, and the two additions below stay on the same side of it: both are single
+plumbing calls returning a fact, not a judgement.
+
+There is also a live piece of evidence for the README's position in this very
+report: the `12 largest` list is already a ranking, and it already misfires. On
+the test suite's own repository (22 changed files, mostly one-line additions) the
+12 shown are `f9.txt f8.txt f7.txt f6.txt f5.txt f4.txt f3.txt f2.txt f18.txt
+f17.txt f16.txt f15.txt`, and `a.txt`, `b.txt` and `deep/nested/d.txt` are all
+omitted. On the 20,000-file synthetic repository every entry ties at `+2 -0` and
+the twelve shown are whichever paths sort last under `LC_ALL=C` reverse
+collation. When magnitudes tie, "the 12 largest" is an arbitrary sample presented
+in the register of a finding. That is the README's own objection to rankings,
+applying to a section it ships.
+
+**Addition 1, recommended: divergence from the branch's own upstream.**
+Not supplied by the CLI (nothing in the block concerns remotes except the base
+branch name). Cost: one guarded plumbing call, `git rev-parse --verify -q
+@{upstream}` then `git rev-list --left-right --count @{upstream}...HEAD`, roughly
+5 ms on the numbers in section 5, and about 50 bytes emitted only when the answer
+is not `0 0`. The decision it changes: whether a push is going to be rejected.
+orient today reports position against `main`, which an agent reads as its whole
+remote situation; a branch 3 ahead of `main` can still be 2 behind
+`origin/<itself>` because someone else pushed, and `git push` will then fail
+non-fast-forward. Unattended runs that end in a push are exactly this project's
+own operating context. The no-upstream case is worth the same line: it tells the
+agent that its push needs `-u`, which it otherwise discovers by failing.
+
+**Addition 2, weaker but defensible: whether the stash stack is non-empty.**
+Not supplied. Cost: the existence of `$git_dir/refs/stash` plus, if present, `git
+rev-list --count refs/stash`; effectively free. The decision it changes: whether
+`git stash pop` is unambiguous. This is the same category as HALT, work parked
+mid-flight and invisible in `git status`, and in a container where several
+worktrees share one `refs/stash` (the arrangement this branch is running under) a
+blind pop destroys a sibling's work. I rate it below addition 1 because the agent
+usually only reaches for the stash when told to, whereas it pushes unprompted.
+
+**Rejected on measurement, not taste.** Working-tree dirty state (supplied,
+probe A). Base branch name (supplied). Submodule status (`git submodule status`
+recurses; not cheap, and the failure it prevents is rare). Anything about
+untracked file *contents*, test commands, or project layout: not git's knowledge,
+and `CLAUDE.md` already owns it.

+Wall clock around the whole hook, `date +%s%N` either side of `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<dir>
+/bin/sh hooks/orient.sh </dev/null >/dev/null`, warm page cache, this container
+(Linux 6.12.76-linuxkit under Docker on the operator's machine).
+
+| repository | n | min | median | p90 | max |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| `/tmp` repo, clean and level (emits nothing) | 20 | 8 ms | 9 ms | 9 ms | 9 ms |
+| `/tmp` repo, 1 ahead, 2-file diff | 20 | 10 ms | 10 ms | 11 ms | 12 ms |
+| `/tmp` repo, 30-file diff | 20 | 10 ms | 10 ms | 11 ms | 11 ms |
+| `/tmp` repo, truncating payload (14 long paths) | 20 | 10 ms | 10 ms | 11 ms | 11 ms |
+| this orient worktree on `/workspace` (level, silent) | 20 | 18 ms | 19 ms | 20 ms | 22 ms |
+| clone of the largest repo reachable (`/workspace/UsageFoundry`, 473 commits, 310 tracked files), 1 ahead, 2-file diff | 20 | 13 ms | 15 ms | 16 ms | 20 ms |
+| same clone, base forced to the root commit: **473 ahead, 310-file diff** | 10 | 78 ms | 79 ms | | 85 ms |
+| synthetic repo, **20,000-file diff** | 10 | 130 ms | 134 ms | | 148 ms |
+
+Measured against the claim at `hooks/orient.sh:8` ("49-123ms on real
+repositories"): on this machine the ordinary cases are **8 to 22 ms**, four to ten
+times faster than the low end of that range, and the range's upper end is only
+approached when the diff itself is large: 79 ms at 310 changed files, 134 ms at
+20,000. The claim is not wrong so much as measured on different hardware; the
+shape it describes (dominated by process spawn, insensitive to history depth,
+sensitive to diff width) is exactly what I see. Note the `/workspace` bind mount
+costs about 10 ms over `/tmp` for identical work, which is the single largest
+factor in the small cases.
+
+**The 10 s timeout in `hooks/hooks.json` is comfortable, not tight.** The worst
+case I could construct, a 20,000-file diff, uses 1.5% of it, a 74x margin. The
+plausible ways to spend 10 s are not diff width: a network filesystem, a
+cold-cache first read of a very large pack, or a repository an order of magnitude
+past anything on this machine. `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` at `hooks/orient.sh:40`
+removes the one unbounded wait I would otherwise expect, blocking on `index.lock`.
+I would not reduce the timeout: the cost of it being generous is zero, and the
+cost of a truncated hook is a silently empty payload.

+`/workspace/orient` (the operator's checkout, branch `main`, same commit
+`c681b2d`) has **uncommitted** modifications to `README.md`, `hooks/orient.sh` and
+`test/run-tests.sh`. My session's own `SessionStart` payload came from that

+Level with origin/main at c681b2d — nothing on this branch yet.
+```
+
+The variant adds a linked-worktree section, reports the 0/0 case instead of
+staying silent, renames `paths_printed` to `repo_text`, and reworks the fence
+wording. Its README is updated in step, including the replacement of "emits
+**nothing at all**" at `README.md:102` and a claim of 24 assertions.
+
+I exercised the variant by hand as well, from a copy at
+`/tmp/orient-ded579862da8-1/orient-worktree-variant.sh`, so as not to touch the
+operator's checkout. It behaves as intended: the worktree case emits `This is a
+linked worktree of /tmp/.../run-wtvariant/wthost; the branch below is checked out
+here and nowhere else.` (364 bytes), and a clean level checkout now emits 180
+bytes instead of 0. Two measured observations about it, offered as evidence and
+not as a request to change anything:
+
+- **Its rationale for reporting 0/0 is half wrong on this CLI version.** The new
+  comment argues that "The base *ref* and the fork point are not in the CLI's own
+  context at any position". The fork point is not (probe F, confirmed). The base
+  ref name **is**, as `Main branch (you will usually use this for PRs)`, and it
+  agreed with orient's own resolution in probes A, F and G. The rest of the
+  argument, that a freshly cut worktree branch is 0/0 by construction and is
+  every isolated agent run's first cycle, is unaffected and is a real gap the
+  committed version leaves.
+- **On a detached HEAD it emits both refusal and position:** `HEAD is detached at
+  ad69a74 — commits made here will not land on any branch.` followed by `Level
+  with main at ad69a74 — nothing on this branch yet.` The phrase "nothing on this
+  branch yet" is applied where the previous line has just said there is no
